subject.title: [Feature]: System prompt architecture refactor — from fragmented rules to unified cognitive framework

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a repository-wide cognitive-framework prompt philosophy and move named operational/safety rules from prompts into runtime enforcement, and what benchmark must demonstrate that it improves outcomes across supported providers?
rationale: The requested work changes how all agents are instructed and where safety and operational constraints are enforced; source-level implementation cannot determine the intended cross-provider tradeoff or acceptance bar.

options.title: Run a bounded evaluation first
options.body: Define representative multi-step tasks, providers, prompt-size measurements, and safety/compatibility assertions before authorizing any architecture change.

options.title: Approve incremental reductions only
options.body: Keep the current architecture and accept narrowly measured removals or dynamic injection changes without adopting a universal cognitive framework.

options.title: Adopt the framework direction
options.body: Sponsor a design proposal that specifies precedence, provider behavior, safety enforcement coverage, migration, and evaluation ownership before implementation.

recommendation.title: Run a bounded evaluation first
recommendation.body: Define representative multi-step tasks, providers, prompt-size measurements, and safety/compatibility assertions before authorizing any architecture change.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion itself identifies this person as the expected product-direction decision point.
